subject.title: `doctor --fix` silently drops the `plugins.allow` entry for a bundled→externalized plugin (codex), unregistering the agent harness — and the gateway still reports healthy

question: When a configured agent selects a harness that is not registered, should gateway readiness become unhealthy, and how should valid fallback runtimes affect that decision?
rationale: The allowlist deletion is a mechanical regression, but readiness semantics affect monitoring and availability for configurations where a missing preferred harness may still have an intentional usable fallback.

options.title: Degrade required runtimes
options.body: Mark readiness unhealthy only when an agent's effective selected runtime is unavailable and no configured valid fallback can execute the turn.

options.title: Warn outside readiness
options.body: Keep readiness process-oriented and surface the missing harness prominently through doctor, status, diagnostics, and update completion instead.

options.title: Fail any missing harness
options.body: Mark readiness unhealthy whenever any configured agent names an unregistered harness, regardless of fallback availability.

recommendation.title: Degrade required runtimes
recommendation.body: Mark readiness unhealthy only when an agent's effective selected runtime is unavailable and no configured valid fallback can execute the turn.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this contributor to plugin doctor behavior, runtime requirement collection, and the missing configured-plugin repair path.
